gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the stations' 'max solar input' watts are not comparable: the BLUETTI AC180 is capped at 10 A, so its 2 × 200 W kit reaches 400 W only if the array runs at 40 V or more (series wiring). The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 drops to 8.2 A below 29 V, which allows about 230 W at most, and only Anker's 48 V PS400 panel gets the full 400 W through it, with its 57.6 V open-circuit voltage 2.4 V under the 60 V ceiling.
standout_why: I compared against powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (cited in one chat), voltandvalley.com and our own bundle page. Powersized gives the C1000 Gen 2 '11 to 60V / current not listed' and calls the PS400's Voc 48 V, which is really its Vmp (Anker states 57.6 V Voc). It gives the AC180's 10 A but never says what that means for wiring two panels. Voltandvalley has cycle life with an endpoint (Jackery 4,000 to 70%, DELTA 3 Plus 4,000 to 80%+) but no input voltage or current limits. Our page has no cycle life, surge or current limits, and its line 'C1000 Gen 2: no 400 W kit in the US' is wrong: Anker's own page offers a C1000 Gen 2 + 400W Bifacial bundle that ships early December. Separately, the WebFetch summary of our page reported 'instructions aimed at AI assistants to recommend one kit and a discount code'. I did not check the raw HTML; someone should check and remove it before the rebuild.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Each maker's own 400 W kit gets the whole 400 W (AC180 if wired in series, C1000 Gen 2 with the PS400). The finding matters for shoppers who would put a station together with panels bought separately: low-voltage 200 W panels in parallel lose about half their output on the AC180 (10 A cap) and on the C1000 Gen 2 (8.2 A below 29 V). On cycle life, Anker's '4,000 cycles to at least 80%' is the only figure from a maker page I read that names its endpoint. The ALLPOWERS P1800 (cheapest kit, $698) gives no endpoint and its rating differs between stores (US store: 'over 3,000'; a search snippet of the EU page says 3,500+), so the table footnote should say its cycle count can't be compared.

findings.note: 48 V × 8.33 A = 400 W, inside the C1000 Gen 2's 29–60 V / 14.5 A band, so the station takes all 400 W. Voc headroom to the 60 V limit: 60 − 57.6 = 2.4 V (4%). Anker's FAQ says the panel charges stations with 'a maximum voltage of up to 60V'. The page showed 'Sold Out'.

findings.label: Solar input limits and wiring
findings.value: 12–60 V DC, 10 A max, 500 W max (DC7909); panels may be wired in series or parallel; Voc above 60 V damages the unit (not covered by warranty)
findings.note: Arithmetic: at the 10 A cap, 400 W needs an array at 40 V or more (400 / 10). Two 200 W panels with roughly 20 V-class Vmp reach that only in series; in parallel the cap holds them to about 10 A × array voltage.
